clue.text: Man presses to contain European anger about bishop's sacred work

parts.note: a king is a man, the chess piece

indicators.note: the word for presses holds the European letter within it

parts.note: jams means presses or crams

indicators.note: the word for anger is placed round the bishop's letter

parts.note: bile is ill temper or anger
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A man squeezes a furious European into a cleric's holy book, or so the scene suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1611 English translation of the scriptures authorised by the Stuart monarch is the classic sacred work of the English-speaking church.

clue.text: Venomous sort caught wearing half-torn item of hosiery over lingerie

indicators.note: half of the hosiery word is torn away, leaving only its second half

parts.note: a stocking is an item of hosiery
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a bra is an item of lingerie

explanation.surface: Someone caught in a laddered stocking worn over underwear, a snarky tabloid scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-torn' leaves the back half of STOCKING; 'wearing' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's longest venomous snake, native to South and Southeast Asia, is a dangerous poisonous sort.

clue.text: Bottle opener verger keeps hidden

indicators.note: the words opener verger keep the answer concealed across their junction

explanation.surface: A church verger secretly holds on to a bottle opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like the thing being opened, but it is the definition in its British sense of courage.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang bottle means courage or daring, as does steady composure under pressure.

clue.text: Starting rotten fish, but not one in extreme condition

parts.note: starting, as when startled, means jumping
off means rotten, of food gone bad

indicators.note: the fish word loses the letter for one

parts.note: plaice is a flatfish
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Beginning to eat a rotten fish, though nobody is in a terrible state yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starting' is not the definition but JUMPING; the definition is the final 'extreme condition'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionaries give the phrase as a point of departure or a remote frontier, and figuratively a desperate, extreme state of affairs.

clue.text: Male getting sick prior to track race

indicators.note: the sick word comes before the track word

parts.note: ill means sick
a run is a track, as a ski run

explanation.surface: A man feeling unwell before an athletics race on the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is not a contest here but a channel of water driving a mill.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill race is the channel carrying water to a waterwheel, and this term is its synonym.

clue.text: Song made by Cliff just after personal problem — nasty

indicators.note: the word for just comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff
BO, body odour, is a personal problem
rough means nasty or unpleasant
fair means just

explanation.surface: A song written by Cliff Richard soon after an unpleasant private trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cliff' looks like the singer Cliff Richard, but it is SCAR, a crag. BO is body odour.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional English ballad was made famous by Simon and Garfunkel in 1966.

clue.text: Literally, none here forced into swallowing alcoholic drink

definitions.note: read literally, none is N ONE, the N1 postcode district of this area

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the drink word inside them
the letters of into are forced into a new order

parts.note: a sling is a gin-based cocktail

explanation.surface: Nobody here was made to knock back strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' rearranges INTO as ITON, which surrounds SLING. Read 'none' literally as N ONE: N1 is the London postcode of this inner-north London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: This north London borough is covered by the N1 postcode, the place where N one applies.

clue.text: Miss having article translated from English into French in Channel Island

indicators.note: the English indefinite article is swapped for its French counterpart

parts.note: a miss is a young lady
a is the English indefinite article

explanation.surface: A young woman's piece of writing rendered into French on Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel Island' suggests Jersey or Guernsey, but this island lies in the Bristol Channel. The French for 'a' is UN.
explanation.definitionFit: The small island off the north Devon coast sits in the Bristol Channel, so it is literally a channel island.

clue.text: Former Private Eye editor, for the most part, was ignorant

indicators.note: most of the editor's surname is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: Richard Ingrams edited the satirical magazine Private Eye from 1963 to 1986

explanation.surface: A former satirical-magazine editor was, mostly, ill-informed.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a British satirical magazine. 'was' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic and dialect adjective, the word meant uninformed or knowing nothing.

clue.text: What sounds like vacuous publicity row

indicators.note: emptied, the word like keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: an ad is publicity
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A quarrel that sounds like empty advertising hype.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What sounds' is the definition, sounding meaning measuring depth, not a homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A weighted cord dropped from a ship is used to sound, or measure, the depth of water.

clue.text: Ultimately, courteous partners at table stop one shouting for more crackers

indicators.note: only the final letter of courteous is taken
the partners plug the middle of the shouting word

parts.note: a crier is one who shouts, like a town crier
East and West are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Polite dinner companions silence a loud guest demanding more biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like biscuits but means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is slang for crazy, and the comparative of the slang adjective screwy means crazier.

clue.text: Radical old German engineer extremely lucky to make a comeback

parts.note: Karl Benz was the German engineer who built the first motor car

indicators.note: the end letters of lucky come back, read in reverse
only the end letters of lucky are taken

explanation.surface: A pioneering German car maker, extremely fortunate, stages a revival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' is the chemistry sense, a group of atoms, not an extremist.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a radical is a group of atoms acting as a unit; this one is C6H5CH2.

clue.text: Mix DNA sequence a lot in movement of the young

parts.note: beat means mix, as with eggs
a gene is a sequence of DNA
a ration is a lot, an allotted share

explanation.surface: A biology lab instruction to combine genetic material, found in a youth trend.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1950s literary and cultural movement of young American writers like Kerouac and Ginsberg.

clue.text: One cutting frayed cable, even if it partially insulates shock?

indicators.note: the numeral cuts into the rearranged cable letters
the letters of cable are frayed into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
in archaic usage and can mean if or even if

explanation.surface: An electrician cuts a frayed cable, even though insulation partly guards against electric shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' is a mass of hair, not an electric jolt, and the hairband covers it only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: This hairband sits across the head and partly covers a shock, or mass, of hair.

clue.text: Gods need power to stop old slowcoach holding Jesus up

indicators.note: the power letter plugs the reversed piece
in this down clue the snail holding the exclamation is read upwards
the slow creature holds the exclamation inside

parts.note: a snail is a slowcoach
Jesus! and My! are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: Deities need strength to halt an elderly dawdler who is delaying Christ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jesus' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'. 'up' turns the whole snail-and-exclamation piece upwards in this down clue before the power letter goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelve principal deities of Greek myth lived on Mount Olympus and were named after it.

clue.text: Indication of which station to stop at

definitions.text: Indication of which station to stop at

parts.words: Indication of which station to stop at
parts.note: seems to be about a railway journey, but means the number that tells a tuner which broadcasting station to stay on

explanation.walkthrough: 'station' suggests trains; here it is a broadcaster, and 'stop at' means tune to.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster's transmission is identified by its frequency, which a listener tunes to in order to hear that channel.

clue.text: Bottom halves of paving stones damaged square flags

indicators.note: the letters taken are damaged into a new order
in this down clue the lower halves of paving and stones are their last three letters

explanation.surface: Cracked paving slabs in a town square where flags are flown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom halves of' takes ING and NES, and 'damaged' rearranges them as ENSIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensigns are flags, especially those flown by ships to show nationality.

clue.text: Wife excited about fair English rose

parts.note: OK means fair or middling
up means excited, as in worked up

explanation.surface: A wife is thrilled by a pretty English rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like a flower but is the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose as the past tense of rise means got up, as a sleeper does when coming to.

clue.text: Daisy steers mostly around east Germany on vacation

indicators.note: the shortened steers word goes around the other letters
most of the steers word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: oxen are steers

indicators.note: Germany emptied out, here kept only at its far end

explanation.surface: Cattle wander around a flower meadow while holidaying in eastern Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye is a large white daisy of grassland, Leucanthemum vulgare.

clue.text: Unexpected afterthought to include children's drink

indicators.note: the unexpected word takes in the children's letters

parts.note: snap means unexpected, as a snap election
CH is the abbreviation for children
PS, a postscript, is an afterthought

explanation.surface: A last-minute addition to a party menu: something for the kids to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'children's drink' suggests a soft drink, but the answer is a strong spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: This strong clear spirit, often fruit-flavoured, is a German and Scandinavian alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Spirit of fictional princess about to embrace lover at last

indicators.note: the reversed name holds the lover's last letter
the princess's name is turned about

parts.note: Princess Leia is the Star Wars heroine

indicators.note: only the final letter of lover is taken

explanation.surface: A storybook princess's ghost about to hug her sweetheart at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses LEIA to AIEL, which takes in R.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's The Tempest the airy spirit serving Prospero bears this name.

clue.text: Eggless sex organs external to stout, round 22

indicators.note: the whole construction is turned round
the shortened organs word goes outside the stout word
the egg-shaped letter is taken out of the organs word

parts.note: gonads are sex organs
ale stands for stout, a dark beer

explanation.surface: A crude remark about reproductive organs outside a pint of stout.
explanation.walkthrough: GNADS round ALE gives GNADALES, which 'round' reverses. 22 refers to 22-across.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-reference points to a creature: this is the Malayan gaur, a wild ox.

clue.text: Sensual setter's obsessively obstinate exterior

indicators.note: the obsessive word is on the outside of the setter's letters

parts.note: anal means obsessively fussy and stubborn
setter's is read as setter is, I'M

explanation.surface: A crossword setter with a sensual side hides behind a stubborn, fussy exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves in the third person, so 'setter's' stands for 'setter is', which is I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal as an adjective means physical and carnal, relating to bodily appetite.

clue.text: Religious collection of disused crosses, all damaged

parts.note: dead means disused, as a dead line

indicators.note: the letters of crosses and all are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: A church's hoard of old crucifixes, all in poor repair.
explanation.definitionFit: These ancient Jewish manuscripts found at Qumran form a collection of religious texts.
